ACTION: Antagonizes the contractile action of leukotrienes (LTD4, LTE4) in airway smooth muscle; inhibits bronchoconstriction caused by antigens
USES: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in adults/children >5 yr
Precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, children, geriatric patients, hepatic disease, Churg-Strauss syndrome, acute bronchospasm
DOSAGE AND ROUTES: • Adult/child ≥12 yr: PO 20 mg bid
• Child 5-11 yr: PO 10 mg bid
Administer: • 1 hr before or 2 hr after meals
• Protect from light
SIDE EFFECTS: CNS: Headache, dizziness, suicidal ideation, insomnia, fever
GI: Nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, dyspepsia, hepatic failure, hepatitis
OTHER: Infections, pain, asthenia, myalgia, fever, increased ALT, urticaria, rash, angioedema
PHARMACOKINETICS: Rapidly absorbed, peak 3 hr, 99% protein binding (albumin), extensively metabolized, inhibits CYP2C9 and 3A4 enzyme systems, excreted in feces, clearance reduced in geriatric patients, hepatic impairment, half-life 10 hr
INTERACTIONS: Increase: plasma levels of zafirlukast—aspirin, acetaminophen, observe for side effects
Increase: bleeding risk—warfarin, monitor INR closely
Increase: zafirlukast level—CYP2C9 inhibitors (valproic acid, fluconazole, amiodarone)
Decrease: plasma levels of zafirlukast—erythromycin, theophylline
Drug/Food
Decrease: bioavailability, take 1 hr prior to or 2 hr after a meal
Drug/Lab Test
Increase: ALT
NURSING CONSIDERATIONS: Assess:
• Churg-Strauss syndrome (rare): eosinophilia, vasculitic rash, worsening pulmonary symptoms, cardiac complications, neuropathy; may be caused by reducing oral corticosteroids
• Respiratory status: respiratory rate, rhythm, depth; auscultate lung fields bilaterally; notify prescriber of abnormalities; not to be used for acute bronchospasm in acute asthma

• Hepatic dysfunction: right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, fatigue, lethargy, pruritus, jaundice, and flulike symptoms, discontinue; monitor LFTs; should be measured immediately and the patient managed if needed
• Mental status: depression, suicidal ideation, insomnia; product may need to be discontinued
• Pregnancy/breastfeeding: use only if clearly needed; do not breastfeed, excreted in breast milk
Evaluate:
• Therapeutic response: ability to breathe more easily
Teach patient/family:
• To check OTC medications, current prescription medications that may increase stimulation, do not stop other asthma medications unless instructed to do so
• To avoid hazardous activities because dizziness may occur
• That if GI upset occurs, take product with 8 oz water; to take 1-2 hr after a meal; to avoid taking with food if possible because absorption may be decreased
• To notify prescriber of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, fatigue, jaundice, anorexia, flulike symptoms (hepatic dysfunction)
• Not to use for acute asthma episodes
• To take even if symptom-free
• Not to take if breastfeeding

ACTION: Binds selectively to omega-1 receptor of the GABAA, benzodiazepine receptor complex; results are sedation, hypnosis, skeletal muscle relaxation, anticonvulsant activity, anxiolytic action
CONTRAINDICATIONS: Black Box Warning: Complex sleeprelated behaviors

DOSAGE AND ROUTES: • Adult: PO 10 mg at bedtime; may increase to 20 mg if needed; 5 mg may be used in low-weight persons, use for only 7-10 days
• Geriatric/hepatic dose: PO 5 mg at bedtime; may increase if needed
Administer: • Immediately before bedtime for sleeplessness
• On empty stomach for fast onset
• Store in tight container in cool environment
SIDE EFFECTS: CNS: Lethargy, drowsiness, daytime sedation, dizziness, confusion, anxiety, amnesia, depersonalization, hallucinations, hyperesthesia, paresthesia, somnolence, tremors, vertigo, complex sleep-related reactions: sleep driving, sleep eating
EENT: Vision change, ear/eye pain, hyperacusis, parosmia
GI: Nausea, abdominal pain, constipation, anorexia, colitis, dyspepsia, dry mouth
MISC: Asthenia, fever, headache, myalgia, dysmenorrhea

INTERACTIONS: Increase: effect of zaleplon—cimetidine, use lower dose
Decrease: zaleplon bioavailability—CYP3A4 inducers (carBAMazepine, phenytoin, rifAMPin)
Increase: CNS depression—CNS depressants, monitor closely
Increase: respiratory depression, death—opioids, avoid concurrent use or use lower dose of both
Drug/Food
• Prolonged absorption, sleep onset reduced: high-fat/heavy meal
Drug/Lab Test
Increase: lipids
NURSING CONSIDERATIONS: Assess:
• Mental status: mood, sensorium, affect, memory (long, short term), excessive sedation, impaired coordination, aggression, confusion, hallucinations
• Sleep disorder: type of sleep problem: falling asleep, staying asleep
Black Box Warning: Complex sleep-related behaviors: Assess for previous complex sleep-related behaviors, and do not use with these patients, sleep eating, driving, walking, all while not fully awake
• Respiratory status: Any patient with compromised respiratory system is more prone to respiratory depression
• Beers: avoid in older adults with delirium or at high risk for delirium; potential for worsening or inducing delirium
Evaluate:
• Therapeutic response: ability to sleep at night, decreased amount of early morning awakening
Teach patient/family:
• To avoid driving or other activities requiring alertness until product is stabilized
• To avoid alcohol ingestion, advise prescriber of all other OTC/Rx/herbals taken
Black Box Warning: That product may cause memory problems, dependence (if used for longer periods of time), changes in behavior/thinking, complex sleeprelated behaviors (sleep eating/driving)
• To report continuing insomnia even with product
• That product is for short-term use only and when patient can sleep ≥4 hr, dependence may occur if used for extended periods
• To take immediately before going to bed
• Not to ingest a high-fat/heavy meal before taking
• To be aware that allergic reactions may occur
• Pregnancy/breastfeeding: Identify whether pregnancy is planned or suspected or if breastfeeding

USES: Used in combination with at least 2 other antiretrovirals for HIV-1 infection, prevention of perinatal HIV

Pregnancy, parenteral; breastfeeding, neonates, hypocupremia, neonatal prematurity, renal disease

Wound healing

Syrup:

RNA, serum cholesterol, pregnancy test, urinalysis, serum lipase, amylase

ACTION: Unknown; may be mediated through both dopamine type 2 (D2) and serotonin type 2 (5-HT2) antagonism

IM route

Increase: hypotension—antihypertensives, monitor B/P
